title: In Praise of My Typewriter
summary: The A.I. projects editor at The New York Times uses chatbots every day. But when it’s time to write, he reaches for an Olivetti Lettera 22 from the 1950s.

title: Can Roof Tiles Reduce Indoor Heat? India Is Finding Out.
summary: As temperatures soar, researchers are experimenting with ways to make life more comfortable for the most vulnerable.
caption: Workers installing heat-reflective tiles on a house in the Kanchipuram district on the outskirts of Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India.

summary: Rui Takahashi, 26, has made waves as one of only a few professional athletes to come out as gay in Japan.
authors: Javier C. Hernández and Hisako Ueno

title: The Threat to a Sanctuary for Children of North Korean Defectors
summary: A school in Seoul caters to students whose parents fled North Korea. Neighbors want it gone, and students say it is just one example of the prejudice they face in the South.
caption: Students running laps with teachers before lunch at Yeomyung School in Seoul in November.

title: Puma Shen, Critic of China, Could be the Next Mayor of Taipei
summary: Puma Shen, who has been sanctioned by China for his efforts to prepare civilians for an invasion, could become Taiwan’s next political star if he wins.
caption: Puma Shen, the Democratic Progressive Party candidate for Taipei mayor, campaigning on Friday. He has energized voters in a city long seen as a stronghold for the Nationalist Party.

title: France’s Bookstores, Beloved Curators of Literature, Are in a Deep Crisis
summary: Caught between by rising costs and price regulations, French booksellers are closing at a record pace, depriving new authors of vital shelf space.
caption: Dinali, an independent bookstore in Strasbourg, France, closed this summer after more than half a century in business.

title: Plaque by Plaque, Russia Erases the Memory of the Gulag’s Horrors
summary: The Kremlin’s rehabilitation of Stalin, who presided over the brutal labor camps of the Gulag, has accelerated during Russia’s war in Ukraine.
caption: Aleksandr V. Kolmakov, a historian, at a cemetery near where the authorities removed a memorial plaque to victims of the Gulag, in Yur-Shor, Russia.

title: Spain’s Far-Right Era Ended in 1975. Will This Man Change That?
summary: If the polls are right, Santiago Abascal’s Vox party could become the first far-right group to join a Spanish government since the days of Franco.

title: A Journalist Fights for Free Speech in Egypt, and to Stay Out of Jail
summary: The fate of Lina Attalah and her news outlet, Mada Masr, in two court cases is seen a test of whether the country’s independent press can survive.
caption: Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr, in Cairo this month. The outlet’s fate feels like “a real and imminent danger,” another publication’s editor said.

title: Why Russia Is Erasing Stalin’s Crimes
summary: Across Russia, memorials to victims of Joseph Stalin’s repressive regime are being quietly dismantled as more and more critics of the war in Ukraine are jailed. Our Moscow correspondent Valerie Hopkins takes us to one example of this erasure.
authors: Valerie Hopkins, Coleman Lowndes, Rebecca Suner and Joey Sendaydiego
